Japanese learning metadata
==========================

Pitch-accent data
-----------------

The bundled lexical-metadata.sqlite database contains a compact transformation
of pitch-accent fields from UniDic for Contemporary Spoken Japanese 3.1.1,
published by the National Institute for Japanese Language and Linguistics.
Maito Player uses the New BSD licence option offered by the UniDic project. The
original AUTHORS and BSD files are installed beside this notice.

Source:
https://clrd.ninjal.ac.jp/unidic_archive/csj/3.1.1/unidic-csj-3.1.1/lex_3_1.csv
SHA-256:
642BCEBC4928856ED9C08D72CFE3E17187978B5EBEC13944EAE80C974E922301

Displayed contours describe Tokyo lexical pitch for a dictionary form. Actual
speech may differ because of conjugation, compounds, accent sandhi, focus,
dialect, or acting. The contours are not measurements of the video's audio.

JLPT estimates
--------------

The bundled JLPT N1-N5 labels are derived from
stephenmk/yomitan-jlpt-vocab 2025.08.01.0, which maps Jonathan Waller's JLPT
vocabulary lists to normalized terms and readings. The dataset is distributed
under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0; its licence is installed
beside this notice.

Source:
https://github.com/stephenmk/yomitan-jlpt-vocab/tree/2025.08.01.0
Archive SHA-256:
B475E2605FBF6D5372BD1D16153981F3924A1237715D33DD44F3312F70A61CE5

The JLPT organization has not published official vocabulary lists for the
current N1-N5 test since the 2010 revision. Every label is therefore shown as an
unofficial community estimate and is not endorsed by the Japan Foundation or
Japan Educational Exchanges and Services.

Transformation
--------------

Only normalized spelling, reading, pitch type, and estimated JLPT level are
retained. The deterministic database build, exact source hashes, row counts,
and attribution files are pinned in runtime-dependencies.lock.json. No claim is
made that NINJAL, the UniDic Consortium, Teruaki Oka, Stephen Kraus, Jonathan
Waller, the Japan Foundation, or JEES endorses this application.
